submission.natural_language_explanation: EleutherAI/pythia-70m L3/N1509+ fires on the token that names a concrete referent's appearance or material: colour terms ('red', 'white', 'blue', 'green', 'yellow', 'purple', 'black', 'brown', 'pink', 'orange' reach 0.5-1.3 of max in every frame tested, whether attributive ('the red house', 'a white suit') or predicative ('the door was red')), and material or substance nouns ('iron', 'blood', 'plastic', 'cotton', 'milk', 'water', 'sugar', 'steel' reach 0.3-1.0), regardless of the syntactic slot they fill. It sits at or below zero on gradable, evaluative and abstract words in the very same slot ('good', 'bad', 'large', 'famous', 'strange', 'beautiful', 'important', 'truth', 'method', 'tall', 'quiet': -0.15 to +0.02 of max) and on ordinals and quantifiers ('first', 'second', 'two': 0.2-0.3), so the boundary is 'perceptible property of a concrete referent', not 'any adjective' and not 'any content word'.

rival_explanations: Broader reading: the pole fires on any lexical modifier that fills the noun-phrase slot, so gradable and evaluative adjectives ('the good house', 'a tall man', 'a strange dress') activate it as strongly as colour terms do.

Narrower, lexical reading: the pole is a set of memorised token detectors ('red', 'white', 'first', '40', ' of'), so a rare hue word the model barely represents ('navy', 'beige') and an unseen one ('teal', 'maroon') stay inactive while 'first' fires in any context.

Quantitative reading: the pole tracks specification of a value on any scale, so ordinals, numerals and partitives ('first', 'two', '40', 'one of') fire as strongly as colour terms, while low-frequency hue words stay silent.

readings.explanation: EleutherAI/pythia-70m L3/N1509+ fires on the token that names a concrete referent's appearance or material: colour terms ('red', 'white', 'blue', 'green', 'yellow', 'purple', 'black', 'brown', 'pink', 'orange' reach 0.5-1.3 of max in every frame tested, whether attributive ('the red house', 'a white suit') or predicative ('the door was red')), and material or substance nouns ('iron', 'blood', 'plastic', 'cotton', 'milk', 'water', 'sugar', 'steel' reach 0.3-1.0), regardless of the syntactic slot they fill. It sits at or below zero on gradable, evaluative and abstract words in the very same slot ('good', 'bad', 'large', 'famous', 'strange', 'beautiful', 'important', 'truth', 'method', 'tall', 'quiet': -0.15 to +0.02 of max) and on ordinals and quantifiers ('first', 'second', 'two': 0.2-0.3), so the boundary is 'perceptible property of a concrete referent', not 'any adjective' and not 'any content word'.

Broader reading: the pole fires on any lexical modifier that fills the noun-phrase slot, so gradable and evaluative adjectives ('the good house', 'a tall man', 'a strange dress') activate it as strongly as colour terms do.

Narrower, lexical reading: the pole is a set of memorised token detectors ('red', 'white', 'first', '40', ' of'), so a rare hue word the model barely represents ('navy', 'beige') and an unseen one ('teal', 'maroon') stay inactive while 'first' fires in any context.

Quantitative reading: the pole tracks specification of a value on any scale, so ordinals, numerals and partitives ('first', 'two', '40', 'one of') fire as strongly as colour terms, while low-frequency hue words stay silent.
